title: Bind shared Git source and publication reads to the requested repository
body:
## Archived version and separate fixture correction

This PR was archived at `1f477eda068420788b5b36ef682bc588317d1400` (two commits). Its first hosted plan job had eight fixture failures. The later fixture correction was not included in this merge and is submitted separately as [PR #5123](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5123), head `95f875490c9d8d198ac594991962c4b2ebc8e017`.

The separate correction adds the standalone fixture helper and restores the exact historical checker only inside disposable source-role fixtures. All37 affected tests pass normal/optimized, and37 optimized tests pass on fresh20a1. PR5123 hosted plan now passes; two historical replay jobs fail at inherited source-pin checks, independently reproduced against exact parent20a1 bytes. No frozen package or pin is changed.

**This PR introduces a real historical-package source-drift rejection:** `research/isolated-descendant-bytecode --check-only` now rejects `scripts/check_research_commit.py`, which remains a pinned input. Expected SHA256 `ecf206a82bf1f4e748efb6cc639919582050d173b3537ec12f7265a4f7b55ead`; current SHA256 `28fed1e156fe8601633ed453f682a158cb15e94981e6c89ed96ae72ffc9d0c6f`. This is not a pre-existing failure and is not suppressed by the fixture correction. No green historical scientific replay is claimed.

An inherited `GIT_DIR` could make the publication checker compare one checkout's working bytes with another repository's HEAD. A dirty checker then passed if those bytes matched the foreign publication; export also selected the foreign commit. Bind the shared Git source/publication subprocesses to the repository discovered from their explicit working directory.

The policy reuses the existing package-local approach in `research/t74-2530-source-partner-audit/audit_common.py`. It removes inherited repository/index/object-directory selection and command-line configuration injections while retaining the existing replacement-ref guard. The history helper and local overlap inventory use the same policy. Actual linked worktrees still work; parent and package-verifier environments remain unchanged. No frozen sources, source pins, selected metadata or mathematical claims change.

Validation on macOS/Darwin27.0 arm64, CPython3.12.7, Git2.44.0:

- Eight new real-Git methods fail against the original code and pass after the fix. They cover dirty-publication and foreign-pin rejection; exact exported commit/payload; history; shared readers/scaffolding; HEAD/planner/overlap inventories; a real linked worktree; inherited selection channels; and unchanged parent/verifier environments.
- All143 targeted compatibility methods pass under normal and optimized Python, with no platform skips: Git readers/replacements/deadlines/spelling, source history, committed-byte checks, exporters, overlap CLI and sparse/plan checks. Normal was132+11 methods; optimized was143 together.
- A nine-file archive from exact committed bytes passes24 tests in each mode from a read-only directory without `.git`. All exported bytes remain unchanged. Git is still available for the tests' disposable repository fixtures; this is not Git-absent execution. Restoring the old Git environment helper in a disposable copy makes the optimized dirty-publication regression fail again.

The shared-tooling change has no registered research-package manifest, so the package exporter is inapplicable; the handoff records a `git archive` closure with every file checked against its committed blob. Native Windows was not executed, nor were scientific packages or the whole archive replayed. The existing `isolated-runner-successor` stale selected-result pin remains outside scope and is not repinned or suppressed.

[Policy, evidence, caller inventory and open questions](docs/research/git-repository-root-binding.md). [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19142319).

Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. Retains Douglas Colkitt's shared runner/scaffold, Tekalign's exporter, Nick Petalas's PR3304 history checks, roger-sato's stored-object policy, and the PR2530 package-local environment-isolation prior art. This is a publication correctness repair, not a new scientific result or kappa.

Submission checkpoint: canonical main81e9bd69e4a5b00ba9c713a1620e36d576d5522e and governing guidance unchanged. Complete09:25–09:26UTC coverage:320openPRs,4233Discussionrecords,6824localHEADnotes. Claims are advisory; unpublished work is outside that coverage.
